# Convex hinge weights via one-sided relative entropy

This is an auxiliary extension of the discounted repair estimates. It is not an OC payment. Unlike q log(q/L), the corrected one-sided entropy below permits a convex nonaffine q. Its concentrating-hinge limit exposes an exact crossing cost rather than removing that cost.

## 1. Setting and convex test

Let C be compact and convex, L=min_i A_i positive on C with affine A_i, and d>=1. Let q be a nonnegative finite convex function on a neighborhood of C that has a finite global convex extension; an affine positive-part hinge is an example. Write ell=min_C L>0 and U=max_C L. Define

    F_q(w)=sup_(t>=0) {t q(w)-(exp(t)-1)L(w)}.

Explicitly, F_q=0 if q<=L, and

    F_q=q log(q/L)-q+L

if q>L. The maximizing parameter is t=(log(q/L))_+. On the compact domain it is uniformly bounded by some B. Therefore the globally finite convex function

    max_i sup_(0<=t<=B) {t q(w)-(exp(t)-1)A_i(w)}

agrees with F_q on C. Each expression is convex in w because t>=0 and A_i is affine. The maximum over i selects the smallest A_i=L. In particular F_q is a legitimate full convex-order test even when q is a hinge. As a scalar function of (q,L), it is convex, nondecreasing in q, and nonincreasing in L>0.

## 2. Tuple inequality

Let w_-,w_+ be a feasible endpoint pair, b their midpoint, V=(L_-+L_+)/2, a=V/L(b)<=1, and q_0=q(b)<=q_bar=(q_-+q_+)/2. Put

    delta_F=(F_q(w_-)+F_q(w_+))/2-F_q(b),
    w_q(b)=(q(b)-L(b))_+.

Convexity in the scalar pair and monotonicity give

    delta_F >= F(q_bar,V)-F(q_0,L(b))
            >= F(q_0,V)-F(q_0,L(b)).

If q_0<=L(b), delta_F>=0 and w_q(b)=0. Otherwise both terms on the last line use the positive branch, and their difference is exactly

    q_0 log(1/a)-L(b)(1-a)
      =(q_0-L(b))log(1/a)
          +L(b)[log(1/a)-(1-a)]
      >=w_q(b)log(1/a).

The final inequality uses -log a>=1-a for 0<a<=1. Thus, with the zero-weight convention,

    w_q(b)(1-a^d)
       <=w_q(b)[1-exp(-d delta_F/w_q(b))]
       <=d delta_F.                                      (1)

No equality q_0=q_bar is presumed.

## 3. Same selected repair, endpoint budget

Suppose pi is the already selected discounted coupling, pi_old has the same two endpoint marginals gamma_-,gamma_+, and rho_old<=cx rho=b_#pi. Its exact error is E=b_#((1-a^d)pi). Define

    Delta_old=(1/2) integral F_q d(gamma_-+gamma_+)
                       -integral F_q d rho_old,
    T_end=(1/2) integral w_q d(gamma_-+gamma_+).

The integrated new gap Delta is nonnegative and at most Delta_old, by the global convex test above. Also w_q=(q-L)_+ is convex on C and has a finite global convex extension. Midpoint Jensen gives

    T:=integral w_q d rho <= T_end.

Weighted Jensen in (1), followed by monotonicity of
T(1-exp(-d Delta/T)) in both nonnegative variables, proves

    integral w_q dE
       <=T_end[1-exp(-d Delta_old/T_end)]
       <=d Delta_old.                                    (2)

If T_end=0 the left side is zero; the nonlinear right side is interpreted as zero. The same coupling works for every q: no new selection is performed. The total form after normal/parity assembly follows by the positively homogeneous concave budget function, as in the earlier repair theorem. The baseline still has factor 2^n; this error budget acquires none.

For an actual prescribed source nu<=cx rho_old and eta=(gamma_-+gamma_+)/2, one may replace Delta_old by

    S_F=integral F_q d eta-integral F_q d nu>=0.

This retains all extra hypotheses needed to identify the actual endpoint branch and its capacity. Generic self-pairing remains numerically trivial.

## 4. Concentrating hinges and the exact crossing penalty

Fix an affine margin h_0(w), set h=(h_0)_+, and use q=k h, k>0. Let

    G_h=h log(h/L)-h,  with 0 log 0=0.

There is the uniform exact bound on C

    0 <= F_(kh)/k-h log k-G_h <= U/k.                    (3)

If kh>L, the difference is L/k. If kh<=L, write t=kh/L in [0,1]. The difference is (L/k)t(1-log t), which lies in [0,L/k]. Thus (3) also covers h=0 without any limit convention beyond continuity.

Let the coupling mass be m and define the old hinge gap and continuous remainder

    C_h=(1/2) integral h d(gamma_-+gamma_+)-integral h d rho_old >=0,
    Delta_G=(1/2) integral G_h d(gamma_-+gamma_+)-integral G_h d rho_old.

Equation (3) gives

    Delta_old(k)/k = C_h log k+Delta_G+O(mU/k).            (4)

This is a rigorous uniform expansion; no differentiating a convex-order inequality is used. When h_0(w_-),h_0(w_+) have strictly opposite signs, the pointwise hinge gap is exactly

    (1/2) min(|h_0(w_-)|,|h_0(w_+)|).

It is zero otherwise. Hence C_h is precisely the integrated cancellation across the cap boundary, with this coefficient. It is not determined merely by the two cap probabilities.

For C_h>0, the concentrating-weight budget (4) has a logarithmically growing cost. No useful zero-cost localization follows. If C_h=0, then Delta_G>=0, and division of (2) by k followed by k->infinity gives

    integral h dE
       <=T_h[1-exp(-d Delta_G/T_h)] <=d Delta_G,
    T_h=(1/2) integral h d(gamma_-+gamma_+),              (5)

with the same zero convention. Here w_(kh)/k=(h-L/k)_+ converges uniformly to h, and T_end(k)/k converges to T_h; E is the same fixed measure throughout. Every limit is therefore justified on a common compact domain. Convex order and midpoint Jensen also force the new hinge gap to be zero when the old one is zero.

## 5. Scope

The new fact is the finite convex-hinge-weighted estimate (2), which does not require affine q. It does not contradict the earlier warning about the uncorrected entropy q log(q/L); that function need not be convex after a hinge substitution. The nonnegative dual parameter and the correction -q+L are essential here.

Equation (4) identifies the price of concentrating the estimate near a cap. The actual selected-minimum equations have not been shown to make C_h vanish or bound it by sufficient cap credit. Moreover the dormant-defect example has zero physical Jordan flow despite positive inverse-rate defect, so no family of convex tests alone supplies the missing actual branch. These obligations remain explicit.
